sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT Pro
sources.evidence: The contemporaneous December 5, 2024 announcement made o1 pro mode available in the ChatGPT Pro model picker and described it as a version of o1 using more compute. It separately compares o1-preview, o1, and o1 pro mode, without parameter counts or topology.

sources.title: o1-pro model reference
sources.evidence: Exact alias maps to o1-pro-2025-03-19. Last documented specifications: 200,000 context, text/image input, text output, reasoning tokens and function calling. Responses and Batch supported. Both alias and snapshot are marked shut down. No total or active parameter count, topology, or exact prompt-cache support is documented.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog: March 19, 2025
sources.evidence: The March 19, 2025 entry announces o1-pro for Responses and Batch as a higher-compute version of o1. This dates the API release separately from the December ChatGPT offering.

sources.title: Model Release Notes: o3-pro, June 10, 2025
sources.evidence: June 10 notes explicitly name o1-pro as the existing ChatGPT model replaced by o3-pro and compare its academic performance and reliability. These exact-variant comparisons disclose no total/active count or architecture. The same-underlying-model statement concerns o3-pro and o3; it cannot establish o1-pro topology.

sources.title: OpenAI o1 System Card, December 5, 2024
sources.evidence: Read introduction, training, checkpoint scope and technical terminology. It covers o1 and o1-mini, with near-final and December 5 o1 checkpoints; the footnote distinguishes the later December 17 update. No exact o1-pro name, total/active parameter count, or structural topology is disclosed. Do not treat this card as a specification of the March Pro snapshot.

sources.title: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini System Card
sources.evidence: The April 16, 2025 card describes large-scale reinforcement learning and includes o1 safety comparisons. Its full extracted text contains no exact o1-pro name and no o1-pro parameter or topology disclosure. Sibling specifications are not transferred.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: The later full GPT-5 card and its comparison tables were checked for o1-pro and technical disclosures. No exact o1-pro name or parameter/topology disclosure was found in the extracted text; GPT-5 pro inference details do not establish o1-pro internals.

sources.title: Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models
sources.evidence: The paper explains o-series safety-specification supervision and reinforcement learning, with o1 evaluations. It does not identify o1-pro or disclose its parameter count or architecture. Exact-name searches for first-party training and interpretability evidence did not locate an additional structural disclosure.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: The guide explains key/value-state caching, including rules for models before GPT-5.6, but does not bind that behavior to o1-pro. Combined with the lack of exact caching support in the model reference, this is insufficient for a qualified Transformer inference. Absence of a cached-input price is not proof that caching is unsupported.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: The API file-input guide documents PDF parsing into extracted text and page images for vision-capable models. The o1-pro reference separately establishes image input. PDF is therefore classified as an API input format, not a distinct native modality or a claim about the December ChatGPT launch.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited service access and reserve intellectual-property rights. Combined with the hosted o1-pro release and API reference, this supports the descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open checkpoint license.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 legacy-snapshot notice explicitly lists o1-pro-2025-03-19 and alias o1-pro as shut down on October 23, 2026. Specifications in this audit are historical documentation, not proof of a working endpoint.

sources.title: How People Use ChatGPT, Appendix C
sources.evidence: The retrospective timeline lists December 1, 2024 for o1-pro and December 5 for the Pro subscription, conflicting with the contemporaneous December 5 announcement. It also lists January 3 for o3-mini where contemporaneous release notes say January 31. This audit prefers the direct launch announcement and records the conflict. Generic language-model architecture discussion is not exact o1-pro evidence.

sources.title: Models.dev o1-pro record
sources.evidence: The baseline lead uses March 19, 2025, o-pro family, 200K context, image input, tools and reasoning. It was inspected but primary sources independently establish the corrected fields.

name.note: Exact API and later ChatGPT spelling. The original announcement calls the offering o1 pro mode.

family.note: The primary descriptions place this higher-compute variant in the o1 series. Replace the unsupported o-pro grouping.

release_date.note: Earliest public release of o1 pro mode in ChatGPT Pro. The later API alias is bound to o1-pro-2025-03-19; no identical checkpoint or unchanged training across these releases is assumed. The retrospective December 1 date conflicts with the direct December 5 launch, which is preferred.

open_weights.note: The documented offering is a hosted ChatGPT/API service; no downloadable o1-pro weights or open-weight grant is supplied.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted model under OpenAI terms, not an SPDX claim.

parameters_b.note: No numerical total count for the exact variant was found in the original material, later exact-name comparisons, or technical reports checked. More inference compute does not establish more learned parameters.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active parameter count is disclosed for o1-pro. Do not infer it from total parameters, runtime compute, or a sibling.

architecture.note: No exact-variant structural disclosure or exact cache binding was established. Being a higher-compute version of o1 does not alone prove unchanged internals. The generic Transformer discussion and o3-pro same-model statement cannot be transferred. Leave broad topology, dense/MoE structure, and size unknown.

context_window.note: Last documented API context for o1-pro-2025-03-19, in tokens. Not a December 2024 ChatGPT limit or a current endpoint-operation claim.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output. PDF is an API file format converted into text and page images under the vision-model rule. No native audio/video support is claimed; these are historical API specifications.

reasoning.note: Both the initial pro mode and later API release explicitly use additional reasoning compute; the API documents reasoning-token support.

tool_call.note: Function calling is expressly listed for the API variant. This does not imply the original ChatGPT mode had every tool available to later o3-pro.

description.value: Higher-compute version of o1 for reasoning tasks, with text and image input.
description.note: Replaces generic O-series marketing claims with supported variant-level behavior; API input capabilities are distinguished from launch-era ChatGPT in the notes.

patch.description: Higher-compute version of o1 for reasoning tasks, with text and image input.
patch.notes: First publicly available as o1 pro mode in ChatGPT Pro on December 5, 2024. The distinct API identifier o1-pro-2025-03-19 launched on March 19, 2025; identical checkpoints across product releases are not assumed. A retrospective OpenAI usage-paper timeline instead says December 1; the contemporaneous launch is preferred. The 200,000-token context and tool/input support are last documented API specifications for the March 19 snapshot. PDF inputs are converted to text and page images. OpenAI lists o1-pro and its snapshot as shut down on October 23, 2026; o3-pro replaced it in the ChatGPT model picker on June 10, 2025. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed in the primary material checked. Architecture remains unverified: higher inference compute, family lineage, and generic cache explanations do not establish exact o1-pro internals.

summary: Corrected earliest release from the March 19 API debut to the December 5, 2024 ChatGPT Pro launch; retained the API snapshot distinction and recorded the conflicting retrospective date. Corrected family to o1, classified the license as Proprietary, added qualified PDF file input, and replaced the generic description. Confirmed historical API context, reasoning, and function calling. Total/active counts remain undisclosed and architecture unverified after original, later comparison, training, and caching checks. Retain the distinct o1-pro API record; do not collapse it into a service_tier option on the o1 identifier.
